proofs.proof: For every feasible action a, |<a,theta_star>|<=||a||_2||theta_star||_2<=LS by Cauchy-Schwarz and the frozen norm bounds. The independent mean bound also gives |<a,theta_star>|<=B. Thus comparator and selected-action means lie in [-min{B,LS},min{B,LS}]; every nonnegative pseudo-regret summand is <=2 min{B,LS}. Summing yields 0<=R_T<=2T min{B,LS} pathwise. Apply this inequality to the SAME admissible private strategy retained in b1 on r1: actions, privacy parameters, output and T selected-reward observations are unchanged. If its old event is R_T<=C F with probability >=1-delta_conf, intersection with this probability-one inequality gives R_T<=min{C F,2T min{B,LS}} at the same confidence, without algorithm selection or union-bound loss. F denotes exactly the explicit rate inside b1's O expression; C is a retained admissible constant. B=0 or S=0 forces exact zero regret by nonnegativity, while the observation budget remains T. The inequality is valid throughout the contract, but native algorithmic adoption here is restricted to r1, using its retained witness. No positive lower bound or matching minimax saturation threshold follows.
proofs.statement: Pathwise bounded-mean upper cap intersected with retained b1 on r1.

proofs.proof: Condition on the exact retained p1 proof, fixed native pseudo-regret quantity, view/guarantee and online resource. It gives 0<=R_T<=2T min{B,LS} pathwise for every feasible trajectory. If B=0, the independent public bound on every mean forces each comparator and chosen-action mean to be zero. If S=0, theta_star=0 forces the same conclusion. In either case min{B,LS}=0 (L>0 is unchanged), hence each pseudo-regret summand and their sum are exactly zero for every legal instance and history. The same admissible private strategy witnessing b1/b2 on r1 is retained; its actions, selected-reward observations, output protocol, privacy parameters and guarantee are not changed. Its zero-regret event therefore holds with probability one and implies the native confidence requirement. The necessary lower bound 0 is metric nonnegativity, and on this region every admissible strategy has regret exactly zero. This is a matching performance-value bracket, not a lower or upper bound of zero on the observation budget: N remains T. No positive-scale lower bound, full-DP conversion or extension outside r1 is asserted.

domains.definition: Each round reveals a predictable action set $\mathcal A_t\subset\mathbb R^d$; contexts may depend on the past. The parameter $\theta_\star$ is fixed and unknown. $$\|a\|_2\le L\quad(a\in\mathcal A_t),\qquad \|\theta_\star\|_2\le S,\qquad |\langle a,\theta_\star\rangle|\le B.$$ $$Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_\star\rangle+\eta_t,\qquad \mathbb E[\eta_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},a_t]=0.$$ Conditional on the pre-action history and current action, the noise is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian. The boundedness conditions needed for privacy sensitivity also require the actual action-reward pair to satisfy $$\|(a_t,Y_t)\|_2\le\widetilde L\qquad\text{almost surely}.$$ almost surely.

protocols.adversary_information: Follow the model and oracle timing. Current private random realizations are not visible to the environment.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. steps: The learner first observes the current context and action set, then selects $a_t$ and receives only that action’s scalar reward. The released action transcript satisfies joint privacy. Rewards for other actions remain hidden.

The parameters $d,T,L,S,\sigma,B,\widetilde L,\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}},\delta_{\mathrm{priv}},\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ are public. Reward parameters and future information of the admissible environment remain hidden.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
